editorial_note.plain_text: Puritan's operator identifies a historical owner as Austrian inventor Oskar Schmidt. That association is supported, but it does not identify his inventions, company or family. The strongest business candidate is Oskar Josef Schmidt, associated with Polyair; his father was also an Austrian inventor named Oskar Schmidt. Conflicting yacht purchase dates complicate the distinction, although a later account favours a younger owner. No source securely connects the vessel owner with either industrial biography. Personal enrichment and biographies are withheld pending that bridge.

uncertainties: Research cutoff 30 September 2026; accessed 1 October 2026. Inventory preceded Forbes-first research. No pre-existing 1940 dossier was present.

The source-record owner association is not disputed. The unresolved question is which independently documented inventor is the named individual. The junior industrialist is the strongest candidate, with broad name, occupation, geography and period convergence; no middle-name, company, age or family identifier links his history to the vessel.

The senior 1902–1976 inventor is a competing search identity, though the operator's 1980 personal sailing statement favours a younger man. The sources disagree on 1974 versus 1978 purchase; no invented father-to-son yacht succession resolves that conflict. Input dates 1975–1991 remain untouched.

The junior candidate's birth 1935 and father-assisted Polyair founding are retained only as identity leads. No middle name, birth date, birthplace, nationality correction, mortality correction or known-for field is imported from them.

LinkedIn, Instagram and personal-website searches were prioritised. The Austrian Kearney consultant, German pharmaceutical/ZF professionals, Swedish Ecohelix engineer and Austrian/German artists are unbridged namesakes. Direct Kearney LinkedIn retrieval failed. None is proposed.

Facebook, Twitter/X, YouTube and TikTok were checked for the exact name with Austrian/inventor context; no verified target account was found. TikTok blocked direct access. Vimeo, Flickr, Trip Advisor and Zillow were checked; art references and a third-party photographer image were not personal owner accounts. Wikipedia disambiguation and musical-instrument/basketball biographies are not target profiles.

Personal and company websites were tested separately. The Vienna artist website cannot be assigned by name and nationality alone. Polyair/LIM and the named property company remain candidate enterprises, not authenticated businesses of this owner.

All four HNWI fields were independently tested. Manufacturing, an advantaged founding mechanism and historical Founder role have candidate-level positive evidence but fail the target-identity premise. Current principal ownership and allocation also remain unverified. Unknown does not mean no wealth, no inheritance or no continuing industrial interest.

The mandatory origin-sector fallback cannot operate without a securely attributable original sector. Yacht ownership and substantial corporate research expenditure do not independently establish principal personal wealth or portfolio materiality.
